title: Psychodrama in Palliative Care "DramaPall 2"
summary:
Psychodrama is a psychotherapy method that uses dramatic reenactment. Through this form of reenactment, feelings and thoughts become tangible, and the individual is empowered to take action and shape their own life by stepping into the role themselves.

In one-on-one sessions, when conducting bedside interventions, people are represented by objects placed on a tray (“table stage”) (Stadler 2020).
The method’s potential to support people as they cope with their own processes—including the dying process—and to help them develop a sense of their own worth and their options for action aligns with key goals of end-of-life care (Frede 2012; Kratz & Jost 2022). Psychodrama is well-suited to helping individuals become more aware of their own sources of strength and to mentalize (cf. Krüger 2020) and utilize both internal and external processes more effectively. Studies on effectiveness have also demonstrated “significant correlations between symptom improvements and psychodrama therapy” in a clinical context (Kunz-Mehlstaub & Stadler 2018; p. 169).

This is a qualitatively oriented mixed-methods study investigating the effects of psychodrama/monodrama in palliative care.

The goal is to improve the well-being and quality of life of critically ill and dying patients.
To date, psychodrama is not available in palliative care. This study closes that gap in research and care.
conditions: The goal is to improve the well-being and quality of life of people who are seriously ill or dying.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- in palliative care
- life expectancy ≥ 3 weeks
- speaks German
- capable of giving consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Delir
- Koma
- psychotic
- multidrug resistent bacterium
